Let \(\langle (x,y),(x',y')\rangle=x^Ty'+x'^Ty\) be the polar form of \(q\). A generator disjoint from \(Y\) is necessarily a graph
\[
G_A=\{(u,Au):u\in \mathbb F_2^6\}
\]
for a linear map \(A:\mathbb F_2^6\to\mathbb F_2^6\). It is also disjoint from \(X\) exactly when \(A\) is invertible.

On \(G_A\),
\[
q(u,Au)=u^TAu.
\]
Over \(\mathbb F_2\), this vanishes for all \(u\) exactly when \(A\) is symmetric with zero diagonal, i.e. an alternating \(6\times6\) matrix. Thus the eligible \(Z\)'s are precisely the invertible alternating matrices \(A\).

For two such graphs \(G_A,G_B\),
\[
G_A\cap G_B=\{0\}
\]
exactly when \(A+B\) is invertible. So we must count unordered pairs of invertible alternating \(6\times6\) matrices whose sum is invertible.

The number of invertible alternating forms on a \(6\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-space is
\[
\frac{|\mathrm{GL}_6(2)|}{|\mathrm{Sp}_6(2)|}
=2^{3\cdot2}(2^1-1)(2^3-1)(2^5-1)
=64\cdot 7\cdot 31
=13888.
\]

Fix one invertible alternating form \(J\). It remains to count invertible alternating forms \(B\) such that \(J+B\) is also invertible.

Use Möbius inversion on the lattice of subspaces. For a \(d\)-dimensional subspace \(U\),
\[
\mu(U)=(-1)^d2^{\binom d2}.
\]
For subspaces \(U,T\), the conditions
\[
U\subseteq \operatorname{rad}(B),\qquad T\subseteq \operatorname{rad}(J+B)
\]
are compatible exactly when
\[
U\cap T=0,\qquad J(U,T)=0.
\]
If \(\dim U=u\), \(\dim T=t\), then the number of alternating forms satisfying both radical containments is
\[
2^{\binom{6-u-t}{2}}.
\]

Counting the compatible ordered pairs \((U,T)\) gives the table
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
u\backslash t&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
0&1&63&651&1395&651&63&1\\
1&63&1890&8820&7560&1008&0&\\
2&651&8820&16800&5040&336&&\\
3&1395&7560&5040&0&&&\\
4&651&1008&336&&&&\\
5&63&0&&&&&\\
6&1&&&&&&
\end{array}
\]
This table follows by classifying \(U\) by \(s=\dim(U\cap U^\perp)\); for fixed \(U\), the number of possible \(T\)'s is
\[
2^{st}\binom{6-u-s}{t}_2.
\]

Therefore the number of \(B\) with both \(B\) and \(J+B\) invertible is
\[
\sum_{u,t} F(u,t)(-1)^{u+t}2^{\binom u2+\binom t2+\binom{6-u-t}{2}}
=5760.
\]

Thus each eligible \(Z\) has \(5760\) possible \(W\)'s. Since unordered pairs are counted twice,
\[
\frac{13888\cdot 5760}{2}=39997440.
\]

\[
\boxed{39997440}
\]
